item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 9, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory will bring heat index values up to 108 degrees to Benton County on Sunday afternoon.
Heat advisory issued for Sunday with index values near 108. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for Benton County from noon to 8 p.m. CDT on Sunday, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees.
Bella Vista Board of Zoning Adjustment meets August 10. The Bella Vista Board of Zoning Adjustment will consider two variance requests for property owners. Agendas for the other meetings this period are published too.
Bentonville Finance Committee to meet monday. The Bentonville Finance Committee will meet Monday at 5 p.m. The agenda includes consideration of a proposed amendment to the city's fiscal year 2027 budget and a request to approve a professional services agreement for engineering services related to the Coler Mountain Bike Preserve expansion project.
Bella Vista planning bodies to consider rezoning and variance requests. The Bella Vista Board of Zoning Adjustment and Planning Commission will meet Sunday at 4:30 p.m. The zoning board will consider a variance request for a residential property, and the planning commission will review a preliminary plat for a residential development.
Taziki's Mediterranean Café opens in Rogers. Taziki's Mediterranean Café opened at 1771 W. Pleasant Grove Road, Suite 104, in Rogers. The approximately 2,900-square-foot restaurant seats 85 guests and required a $950,000 investment.
Simmons Foods promotes Salmon to chief commercial officer. Siloam Springs-based Simmons Foods promoted Scott Salmon, president of Simmons Pet Food, to the newly created role of chief commercial officer. Jacob Rogers will succeed Salmon as president of Simmons Pet Food.
Walton Family Foundation grants $599,139 to NWACC. The Walton Family Foundation provided a $599,139 grant to Northwest Arkansas Community College to expand its Learning, Improvement, Fun and Empowerment program.
Jessica DeBari named executive director of Community Creative Center. Fayetteville artist Jessica DeBari has been appointed executive director of Community Creative Center, a Fayetteville-based nonprofit arts organization. She succeeds Bryce Brisco, who stepped down in late July.
Fayetteville opens cooling shelters through end of August. The City of Fayetteville committed to keeping a cooling shelter open daily through the end of August, a change made in response to resident feedback about inconsistent access to relief during extreme heat.
Benton County considers one-cent sales tax. Benton County held an intergovernmental meeting to discuss a proposed one-cent sales tax.
Benton County named as candidate for possible nuclear development. A feasibility study presented to Arkansas lawmakers identified a site in Benton County as a candidate for possible future nuclear power development.
Springdale hosts free Saturday picnics through August. The Downtown Springdale Alliance is hosting a weekly Picnic in the Park series throughout August on Saturdays, featuring food, music, and community gathering.
